chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, who said:

I said, 'Can I pray an optional prayer during the time of an obligatory prayer?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, at the beginning of the time, when you are with an Imam whom you follow. So when you are alone, begin with the prescribed prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the correct order for praying optional prayers if they overlap with obligatory prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential nuance of prayer order during overlapping times, distinguishing between congregational settings where following the Imam's pace allows for prior nafl, and solitary worship where the fard takes precedence to ensure its timely fulfillment. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the integrity of obligatory duties while accommodating voluntary acts within their designated windows. The ruling underscores the practical wisdom of prioritizing the mandatory when alone, preventing potential neglect of the fard due to the length of nafl.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Usman Bin Isa, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said, ‘Can I pray an Optional Salāt during the time of an Obligatory (Salāt)?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, during the beginning of the time, when he was with a prayer-leader, following him. So when you were alone, so begin with the Prescribed (Salāt)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Can I perform optional Salah (prayer) in the time for obligatory one?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘Yes, you can do so in the beginning of time if you are with the Imam who leads you in Salah (prayer). If you are alone, then perform the obligatory first.’”
